fields.title: 1. Google — First Dedicated Heavy-Lift Launch for Project Suncatcher on New Glenn
fields.md:
### 1-1. What the primary source says

| Item | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Title · author | 'We're partnering with Blue Origin on our first heavy-lift Project Suncatcher launch' · Travis Beals (Senior Director, Paradigms of Intelligence) · 2026-11-19 | [Google Blog](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-research/blue-origin-project-suncatcher-partnership/) |
| Launch vehicle · timing | New Glenn deploys the satellites · 'Targeted for Q1 2029' | Same as above |
| Orbit · payload | Sun-synchronous orbit · each satellite 'roughly the capacity of a data center rack' | Same as above |
| Not stated | Number of satellites · amount · terms · mention of SpaceX | Same as above |

### 1-2. What press coverage adds (for cross-checking)

| Content | Source |
|---|---|
| Launch site Cape Canaveral · dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit · 'a batch' | ⑥ [SatNews](https://satnews.com/2026/11/19/google-selects-blue-origins-new-glenn-rocket-for-2029-ai-satellite-launch/), 2026-11-19 |
| The first prototype (built by Planet) reached orbit in October · a test linking 2 satellites in 2027 · New Glenn was grounded after exploding during a May test, with its return pushed to January | ⑥ [TNW](https://thenextweb.com/news/google-blue-origin-new-glenn-project-suncatcher-2029), 2026-11-19 |
| The first prototype reached orbit on a SpaceX Transporter-18 rideshare (confirmed by Google on 10/1) · this announcement does not mean SpaceX lost its existing contracts or that all later launches are assigned to Blue Origin | ⑥ [teslanorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/11/19/google-blue-origin-suncatcher-launch/), 2026-11-19 |

### 1-3. Where it touches the judgment layer

- **C-2030-1 (orbital data center revenue > $0)**: This milestone counts only SpaceX's own orbital data center revenue. A competitor's launch schedule is not an input. The record is kept only as a background note to the milestone (source: `state.milestones[C-2030-1].event_note_2026_11_20`).
- **Relationship with Google**: Google is both an AI compute customer of SpaceX (reported — under 10%, terminable with 90 days' notice after 2026-12-31) and a shareholder. This announcement does not address that contract. Changes are viewed only through the 4Q26 10-K customer concentration note and T1's 'SI revenue +$2.76 billion' checkpoint (source: `state.milestones[C-2029-1]` · `state.triggers_next_12m[T1]`).
- **Launch market**: One dedicated heavy-lift launch went to a competitor. The amount was not disclosed, and as it is a 2029 matter it is outside the 12-month trigger window. There is no milestone or rule input (source: table 1-1 · `state.probability_adjustment_rules`).
- **New Glenn schedule**: Amazon Leo has also reserved 24 New Glenn launches. The report that the return was pushed to 2027-01 is recorded in the T4 note (R5 is judged only on whether a plan launches at the end of 2027) (source: TNW, 2026-11-19 · `state.triggers_next_12m[T4]`).
- **Monitor's share (listing only)**: The monitor linked this event to T1. It also linked the funding report from the same cycle to T1, but that is a T5 event (source: `state.triggers_next_12m[T1].log_check`).
